nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order and let $ps$ be a list of $n$ points in $K^2$. Counting one unit of cost per squared distance computed, twice the cost of the brute-force scan on $ps$ equals $n(n-1)$; that is, the scan computes exactly $n(n-1)/2$ squared distances.
nodes.title: Cost of the brute-force closest-pair scan

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order, and write $d(p, q) = (x - x')^2 + (y - y')^2$ for the squared distance between points $p = (x, y)$ and $q = (x', y')$ of $K^2$. On a list $c_1, \dots, c_n$ of points in $K^2$, the brute-force scan returns no value if $n < 2$, and otherwise returns $\min_{i < j} d(c_i, c_j)$: for each $i$ it computes the least squared distance from $c_i$ to the later points…
nodes.title: Brute-force closest pair

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field. For every list of points in $K^2$, the divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm returns the same value as the brute-force scan (their costs may differ).
nodes.title: Divide and conquer agrees with brute force

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field. For every list of points in $K^2$, the divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm returns no value if and only if the list has fewer than two entries.
nodes.title: The closest-pair algorithm returns no value exactly on fewer than two points

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, write $d(p, q) = (x - x')^2 + (y - y')^2$ for the squared distance between points $p = (x, y)$ and $q = (x', y')$ of $K^2$, and let $ps$ be a list of points in $K^2$. If the divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm returns a value $\delta$ on $ps$, then $\delta = d(p, q)$ for some entries $p$, $q$ of $ps$ at different positions. For any two entries $p$, $q$ of $ps$ at different…
nodes.title: The closest-pair algorithm returns the answer

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and let $ps$ be a list of at least two points in $K^2$. Then the divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm returns a value $\delta$, and $\delta$ is the least squared distance between two entries of $ps$ at different positions: some two entries at different positions have squared distance $\delta$, and any two entries at different positions have squared distance at least $\delta$.
nodes.title: Correctness of divide-and-conquer closest pair

nodes.summary: For every list of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the closest-pair algorithm computes at most $7 n \lceil \log_2 n \rceil + n$ squared distances, where $\lceil \log_2 0 \rceil$ is read as $0$. In particular it computes $O(n \log n)$ distances.
nodes.title: Running time of the closest-pair algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order. Given a list of points in $K^2$, the closest-pair algorithm sorts the points by first coordinate (merge sort, at no cost) and runs the closest-pair recursion on the sorted list. It returns a squared distance or no value, and is charged one unit of cost per squared distance computed.
nodes.title: Divide-and-conquer closest pair

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, write $d(u, v) = (x - x')^2 + (y - y')^2$ for the squared distance between points $u = (x, y)$ and $v = (x', y')$ of $K^2$, and let $xs$ be a list of points in $K^2$ sorted by first coordinate: whenever an entry precedes another, its first coordinate is at most the other's. If the closest-pair recursion returns a value $\delta$ on $xs$, then $\delta = d(p, q)$ for some entries…
nodes.title: The closest-pair recursion is correct on lists sorted by first coordinate

nodes.summary: For every list of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ sorted by nondecreasing $x$-coordinate, the divide-and-conquer recursion of the closest-pair algorithm computes at most $7 n \lceil \log_2 n \rceil + n$ squared distances, where $\lceil \log_2 0 \rceil$ is read as $0$.
nodes.title: Running time of the closest-pair recursion

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $c_1, \dots, c_n$ a list of points $c_i = (x_i, y_i)$ of $K^2$. If $n \le 3$, the recursion returns the brute-force scan of the list. Otherwise let $m = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, and run the recursion on $c_1, \dots, c_m$ and on $c_{m+1}, \dots, c_n$. If neither call returns a value, it returns no value. Otherwise let $\delta$ be the least of the returned values, let $T$ be the…
nodes.title: Closest-pair recursion

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field. The squared distance between points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of $K^2$ is $(p_1 - q_1)^2 + (p_2 - q_2)^2$.
nodes.title: Squared distance in the plane

nodes.summary: Given reals $\delta$ and $x_{\mathrm{mid}}$, a tagged point $((x, y), s)$ lies in the strip when $(x - x_{\mathrm{mid}})^2 < \delta$, and moreover $x \le x_{\mathrm{mid}}$ if its side $s$ is left ($s$ false) and $x_{\mathrm{mid}} \le x$ if its side $s$ is right ($s$ true).
nodes.title: Strip points

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, and write $d(p, q) = (p_1 - q_1)^2 + (p_2 - q_2)^2$ for the squared distance between points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of $K^2$. For a list $c_1, \dots, c_n$ of points of $K^2$, an optional value $r$ (an element of $K$ or no value) is an answer for the list when every value $\delta$ that $r$ holds equals $d(c_i, c_j)$ for some $i < j$, and when for all $i < j$, $r$…
nodes.title: Closest-pair answer

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, and write $d(p, q) = (p_1 - q_1)^2 + (p_2 - q_2)^2$ for the squared distance between points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of $K^2$. For a list $c_1, \dots, c_n$ of points of $K^2$, an element $\delta$ of $K$ is the least pairwise squared distance of the list when $\delta = d(c_i, c_j)$ for some $i < j$ and $\delta \le d(c_i, c_j)$ for all $i < j$.

nodes.summary: For a real $\delta$, two tagged points $a$ and $b$ are same-side far apart when, if $a$ and $b$ carry the same side, the squared distance between their points is at least $\delta$.
nodes.title: Same-side points far apart

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be a real, $q = (q_1, q_2)$ a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $L$ a list of points of $\mathbb{R}^2$. The cost of the scan from $q$ over $L$ with threshold $\delta$, one unit per squared distance computed, equals the length of the longest initial segment of $L$ all of whose points $r = (r_1, r_2)$ satisfy $(r_2 - q_2)^2 < \delta$.

The scan from $p$ with…

Let $ys$ be a list of points in $K^2$ sorted by second coordinate: whenever an entry precedes another, its second coordinate is at most the other's. If $a = (a_1, a_2)$ and $b = (b_1, b_2)$ are entries of $ys$ at positions $i < j$…

Then the strip scan with parameter $\delta$ over the underlying points of $Y$ (tags forgotten) computes at…
nodes.title: Cost of the strip scan

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, $\delta \in K$ and $c_1, \dots, c_n$ a list of points of $K^2$. For each $i$, the strip scan runs the strip scan from $c_i$ with threshold $\delta$ on the later points $c_{i+1}, \dots, c_n$. It returns the least of the values these scans return, or no value if none of them returns a value, and its cost is the sum of their costs.
nodes.title: Closest-pair strip scan

nodes.summary: A tagged point is a pair $(p, s)$ of a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and a Boolean $s$, read as the side of the dividing line on which $p$ lies: false for left, true for right.
nodes.title: Side-tagged points

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
